request.spec:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rolling a fiscal year over now also soft-closes every period of the old year that's still open, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

The change is a few lines in `PeriodService.rollover` (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/period/PeriodService.java`). After it writes the `ROLLOVER` audit line, it goes through the old year's periods in start-date order. Any period that isn't already closed or soft-closed gets soft-closed the same way a manual soft close does: its figures are fixed and a `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED` line is written for it. Periods that were already closed are left alone; in the test, `2026-11` stays "yes".

Two things to know:
- **No separate permission check:** the manual soft close checks the sheet's close permission. The rollover only checks that the user is a steward, because only stewards can roll a year over at all.
- **Undo doesn't reopen them:** undoing a rollover still removes the new periods and takes back the opening balances, but the old-year periods it soft-closed stay soft-closed. The request didn't cover undo. If undo should reverse this too, it's a small follow-up.

No front-end change was needed. The rollover screen already reloads the period list from the server's reply, so the "soft" status shows up straight away.
